# Fino1: On the Transferability of Reasoning-Enhanced LLMs and Reinforcement Learning to Finance

arXiv [2502.08127](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08127) · v1 2025-02-12 · latest 2025-06-14

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Improving and evaluating LLMs' financial reasoning (numerical QA over financial texts, tables, long documents and equations) via a CoT corpus, SFT+RL-trained models, and a benchmark. | “To address these gaps, we introduce FinCoT, the first open high-fidelity CoT corpus for finance, distilled from seven QA datasets by a novel three-stage pipeline that incorporates domain supervision, iterative LLM refinement, and difficulty-aware filtering.” |
| **architecture** | Three-stage CoT construction (GPT-4o synthesis with domain guidance, GPT-4o generator/verifier iterative refinement, Llama3.1-8B difficulty filtering), then two-stage training of Qwen3: SFT on FinCoT_SFT then RL (PPO, DPO, GRPO) with GPT-4o-judged multi-part reward. | “Following previous studies [1, 8], a two-stage training approach, supervised fine-tuning and RL, is adopted to develop the model. FinCoT is divided into two parts FinCoT_SFT (7686) and FinCoT_RL (1,500) to support the training.” |
| **data** | FinCoT: 9,186 CoT-annotated QA pairs from FinQA, ConvFinQA, DocFinQA, TATQA, Econ_Logic, DocMath-Eval, BizBench-QA; evaluated on FinReason (FinQA 1,100, DM-Simplong 100, DM-Complong 300, XBRL-Math 90) from financial reports and XBRL filings. | “Building our raw data collection, we further curate the first dataset containing 9,186 chain-of-thought annotated QA pairs, specifically designed to support SFT and RL for financial reasoning models” |
| **window** | No dated period; FinCoT split into 7,686 SFT and 1,500 RL examples; evaluation on separate FinReason benchmark datasets. | “FinCoT is divided into two parts FinCoT_SFT (7686) and FinCoT_RL (1,500) to support the training.” |
| **models** | Backbones Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B (Fin-o1-8B, Fin-o1-14B); GPT-4o used for CoT generation, verification and reward judging; Llama3.1-8B-Instruct for difficulty filtering. | “Qwen3 are selected as backbone models, given their strong performance among small and mid-sized LLMs (shown in Table 3).” |
| **baselines** | 29 LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-o1-preview, GPT-o3-mini, GPT-4.5, DeepSeek-V3/R1, Llama and Qwen families, R1-distills, S1-32B, Limo, FinR1-7B, Dianjin-R1-7B; plus ablations with PPO, DPO, no-CoT SFT. | “we select a diverse set of 29 LLMs from the GPT, LLaMA, DeepSeek, and Qwen families, along with other reasoning models including both general domain and financial specific models.” |
| **headline_result** | Fin-o1-14B average accuracy 61.07 across four FinReason datasets, second only to DeepSeek-V3 (61.30); Fin-o1-8B averages 59.95. | “\| Fino1-14B \| 74.18 \| 55.00 \| 87.78 \| 27.33 \| 61.07” |
